version.changelog: Bring the skill to the current api-gateway baseline and tell the connection-to-function-to-trigger story: the shared Functions and Triggers sections open with an example for this app (a hosted function that performs one action for it through the Maton SDK, and the trigger that runs it - its own event source where it has one, otherwise a time schedule), the description says these constructs turn the connection into automation and add no capability of their own, the passthrough is described by its enforced boundary, CLI and SDK installs are pinned to 0.3.1, absolute API URLs are placeholders, and multipart uploads use mktemp.

llm.summary: This Salesforce skill is mostly transparent, but its hosted automation can run with broad Maton account access beyond a single Salesforce connection, so it warrants review before installation.

dimensions.detail: Network access, OAuth, local credential-store use, and Salesforce record access are expected for this integration. The artifact gives proportional handling guidance, including avoiding credential extraction, defaulting to reads, filtering person-data queries, and confirming writes.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: NPM installation pins @maton/cli@0.3.1, while the Homebrew path installs from the current maton-ai tap and only pins after installation, so users should verify the installed version before authenticating.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions repeatedly require explicit user approval for new connections, writes, deletes, batches, function deploys, trigger destinations, and local --exec handlers. Shared trigger reference files are labeled as platform event-source catalogues that do not widen Salesforce itself.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent elements are disclosed but high impact: OAuth/API credentials are stored locally, hosted functions persist server-side, triggers and destinations can forward events continuously, and function runtime identity is account-wide unless the user deploys from a dedicated least-privilege Maton account.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The Salesforce CRUD, SOQL, OAuth, and connection management capabilities match the stated CRM administration purpose, but the hosted function path is broader: the artifact says functions run with the deploying Maton account identity and can reach the connections that account holds, not only the Salesforce connection for the task.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you need Salesforce CRM administration. Prefer the pinned NPM install or independently verify the Homebrew-installed Maton CLI version before logging in. Use OAuth, narrow Salesforce scopes, sandbox orgs for destructive or batch work, and a dedicated Maton account with only the needed Salesforce connection before deploying hosted functions or triggers. Treat trigger destinations as persistent forwarding and approve writes, deletes, batches, and third-party destinations only after checking exact records and data flow.
llm.findings:
[SDI-4] expected: Downgraded. The inspected HubSpot trigger reference explicitly labels itself as shared Maton platform reference text that does not describe or widen the Salesforce app, matching the main skill's explanation of reference catalogues.
[T05] unexpected: Accepted as a Review concern, not as malicious behavior. The artifact discloses that hosted functions receive a runtime MATON_API_KEY for the deploying account and that the account's connections are what the function can reach; that is broader than a single Salesforce connection and relies on review and dedicated-account practice rather than enforced connection scoping.
[T08] expected: Partially accepted as a supply-chain note. Installing the Maton CLI is expected, and NPM is version-pinned, but the Homebrew command does not guarantee that the initially installed artifact is the reviewed version before credentials are used.
